data.title: UGI to Spin Off Liquefied Petroleum Gas Business
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

UGI plans to spin off its global liquefied petroleum gas business into two public companies.

The distributor of energy products on Wednesday said the spinoff, approved by its board, is part of the company's transformation strategy and should position both companies for long-term growth. The separation is expected to be completed during the second half of 2027.

After the spinoff's completion, the new UGI will be a natural gas infrastructure company for customers in the mid-atlantic regions. The new liquefied petroleum gas company is expected to be a distributor in Europe, while also being a retail propane distributor in the U.S.

Under the proposed spinoff plan, UGI shareholders will retain their current shares and receive a pro-rata distribution of shares of the new LPG company's stock. After the spinoff, the new UGI may retain a stake of up to 20% in the new LPG company.

The spinoff came as UGI on Wednesday posted a fourth-quarter profit of $8 million, or 4 cents a share, compared with a loss of $13 million, or 6 cents a share, the year earlier.

Revenue fell to $1.16 billion from $1.2 billion the year before.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: Nvidia's deeper risks predate Huang's scandal: McGeever
data.description:
By Jamie McGeever

As investors digest the latest twists in scandal-hit Nvidia's evolving drama, it's worth remembering that they had already started to sour on the world's erstwhile AI darling well before former CEO Jensen Huang resigned. That may be far more worrying for the AI trade.

Nvidia offered investors some relief on Tuesday, delivering bumper third-quarter revenue and earnings, as well as sales projections that exceeded Wall Street estimates. Nvidia's shares rose as much as 5% in extended trading.

This comes after Nvidia's share price tanked nearly 40% from its record high on October 6, wiping some $2 trillion off its market capitalization and knocking the firm off its pedestal as the world's most valuable company.

Importantly, the bulk of Nvidia’s share price decline came before Huang admitted on November 8 to having an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed and alleged Chinese spy. His resignation came four days later following allegations of improper relationships with Nvidia employees.

There is suddenly a plethora of reasons why investors may think twice about buying Nvidia shares, such as trust and accountability, the board's leadership, and US national security concerns amid external investigations, including a reported probe by the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

But just as worrying may be the gnawing unease investors have about Nvidia's customer financing, long-term demand for its chips, and the AI business model – all of which predate the scandal.

'DISCIPLINED' APPROACH

Nvidia's fall from favor has been rapid. This should probably come as no surprise, given how meteoric its ascent was.

It is one of only 10 firms since 1960 to hold the title of the largest company in the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX, according to JPMorgan Private Bank's Michael Cembalest. That’s a remarkably small number and would be even smaller were it not for Cisco's three days at the top in 2000.

Nvidia's epic rise was the fastest of them all. Its share of the S&P 500 in December 2022 was 1%. By May this year, it was 8.5%. Revenue and profit growth have exploded thanks to soaring demand for its chips from hyperscalers and so-called “neocloud” AI partners that Nvidia has often helped finance.

It's unclear how committed interim CEO and former chief financial officer Colette Kress is to this model. On the earnings call on Tuesday, she said Nvidia will be “disciplined" and selective in its capital commitments, investments, and guarantees, although she said there are no plans to change its backstops for "neocloud" companies.

Should that position change, however, companies like CoreWeave , Nebius , IREN and Applied Digital , whose shares have already tumbled steeply in recent months, could fall further.

BIS WARNING

This shines a spotlight on the AI vendor financing trend. The Bank for International Settlements published a special report on the subject last month, which found that between 2021 and 2025, nearly 30% of all AI firms’ investment deals by value involved an AI firm on the other side. Meanwhile, 55% of incoming investments in AI firms came from other AI firms.

The authors warned that such circular relationships can artificially inflate demand, which can become a problem if revenue growth and real end-user demand slow. The AI flywheel could then go into reverse, potentially leading to "significant financial market volatility," the BIS warned.

This risk is exacerbated by the fact that many of these deals are opaque, complex, and private, making them difficult to monitor and supervise.

"These risks may be magnified by the growing use of private credit and special purpose vehicles to finance AI infrastructure, which can create hidden leverage and interconnected exposures that amplify financial stress during downturns," the BIS authors wrote.

The AI sector is clearly in a downturn on Wall Street right now, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropping nearly 30% in the last six weeks. AI’s crown jewel may have just released sparkling results, but they are not bright enough to obscure the deep-rooted, mounting concerns about the AI ecosystem.

(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters)

data.title: Palliser builds stake in UK's Chemring and pushes for potential Roke sale
data.description:
Activist investor Palliser Capital called on UK defence company Chemring Group on Wednesday to launch a comprehensive strategic review, including a potential sale or separation of its electronic warfare business, Roke.

  • Palliser has built a stake of about 3% in Chemring, it said

  • The Financial Times reported earlier in the day, citing a letter by Palliser to Chemring, that the activist investor believed Roke should be sold off and could be valued at roughly £600 million to £730 million ($792 million to $963 million) on its own

  • Palliser asked Chemring to accelerate investment in its energetics unit that tests single-use explosive, propellant, and pyrotechnic devices

  • It also urged expansion in the US and other international markets

  • Chemring said in a statement that it welcomed engagement with shareholders but does not comment on media or market speculation

  • The defence group earlier this month reported fiscal year 2026 adjusted earnings before interest and tax slightly below market expectations and launched a strategic review of its US sensors business

  • Shares of the company jumped 2.3% following the FT report

($1 = 0.7578 pounds)

data.title: US FDA approves Regeneron's drug for generalized myasthenia gravis
data.description:
The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Regeneron Pharmaceuticals' drug to treat adults with a type of rare autoimmune disease called generalized myasthenia gravis, the company said on Wednesday.

The drug, cemdisiran, branded as Livsayis, was approved for adults with generalized myasthenia gravis who test positive for anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies, the most common form of the disease.

Generalized myasthenia gravis causes muscle weakness affecting movement, speech, swallowing and breathing.

Livsayis, which is to be injected under the skin once every three months, is the only US-approved treatment for the disease, Regeneron said.

data.title: PANW Stock Soars 11% After-Hours On Q1 Earnings Beat, $4.5B Acquisition Announcement
data.description:
Key points:
  • Total revenue for the quarter reached $3.44 billion, outpacing consensus forecasts, while earnings per share hit $1.05. 
  • Applied Compute acquisition to bolster PANW’s enterprise capabilities in open-weight AI models. 
  • Palo Alto expects full-year revenue at $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock gained about 11% after-hours on Wednesday after topping analyst expectations for its first quarter ending October, along with a raised outlook on the backdrop of concerns regarding artificial intelligence-powered cyber threats.

For the fiscal first quarter, the company reported earnings of $1.05 per share, beating analysts' $0.97 estimate.

Total revenue surged 39% to $3.44 billion, up from $2.47 billion during the same period last year and beating expectations of $3.31 billion.

Annual recurring revenue (ARR), the yearly income a subscription or contract business expects from active customers, climbed 66% year-over-year to hit $9.73 billion. ARR is one of the key metrics analysts use when evaluating companies like Palo Alto.

“As AI reshapes the threat landscape, we must continually evolve to protect our customers and enable them to adopt AI securely,” CEO Nikesh Arora said in a release.

A wave of recent high-profile system outages that hit financial institutions, airlines, and enterprise infrastructure have prompted businesses to significantly boost their digital security investments, directly aiding cybersecurity firms like Palo Alto Networks and its peers like Zscaler (ZS) and CrowdStrike (CRWD).

The $4.5 Billion Applied Compute Deal

Palo Alto Networks announced an agreement to acquire Applied Compute, an AI model platform, in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion.

Applied Compute provides an infrastructure environment enabling enterprises to train, refine, and deploy open-weight artificial intelligence models and autonomous agents. By opting for open-weight systems over proprietary closed frameworks, organizations can download and run model parameters directly within their private infrastructure, creating a tailored, budget-friendly approach with enhanced data governance.

“If it works, I think this will dwarf the ability that we have in cybersecurity,” Arora said on an earnings call. “This could be bigger than what we do.“

Q2 and Full-Year 2027 Outlook

For the upcoming second quarter ending January 2027, the cybersecurity stock expects its total revenue to be in the range of $3.530 billion to $3.550 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 36% to 37% and above analyst expectations.

For the full year, it expects revenue in the range of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion, above expectations of $14.16 billion.

data.title: Plurilock Security Inc. Announces Shareholder Approval for Plan of Arrangement with Quantum eMotion Corp.
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Plurilock Security Inc. (OTCQB: PLCKF) ("Plurilock" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that, at the special meeting (the "Meeting") of holders (the "Shareholders") of common shares of Plurilock (each, a "Plurilock Share" and, collectively, the "Plurilock Shares") held on November 18, 2026, Shareholders voted in favour of the special resolution (the "Arrangement Resolution") approving the previously announced plan of arrangement (the "Arrangement") with Quantum eMotion Corp. ("QeM"). The Arrangement is being completed pursuant to the terms and conditions of a definitive arrangement agreement between Plurilock and QeM dated September 28, 2026 (the "Arrangement Agreement").

Under the Arrangement, QeM will acquire all of the issued and outstanding Plurilock Shares. Shareholders will receive C$0.084 in cash and 0.0763 of a common share of QeM (each whole common share of QeM, a "QeM Share") in exchange for each Plurilock Share they hold (together, the "Consideration"), implying total consideration of C$0.28 per Plurilock Share. Further, all outstanding options to acquire Plurilock Shares ("Plurilock Options") will be cancelled in exchange for QeM Shares and cash in the same proportions as the Consideration having a value equal to the amount (if any) by which C$0.28 exceeds the applicable exercise price per Plurilock Option. All outstanding restricted share units will vest immediately prior to the effective time of the Arrangement and be settled for the Consideration. All outstanding warrants and convertible debentures of Plurilock will, in accordance with their terms and without further action by the holders thereof, entitle the holders to receive, upon exercise or conversion, the Consideration in lieu of Plurilock Shares.

Shareholders holding a total of 68,226,137 Plurilock Shares were represented in person or by proxy at the Meeting, representing 60.38% of the 112,989,001 issued and outstanding Plurilock Shares entitled to vote as of October 1, 2026, the record date for the Meeting.

The Arrangement required the approval of: (i) at least two-thirds (66⅔%) of the votes cast by Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote at the Meeting; and (ii) a majority of the votes cast by Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote at the Meeting, excluding Plurilock Shares held by "interested parties" as defined in Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101").

At the Meeting, 99.58% of the votes cast by Shareholders (99.54% after excluding Plurilock Shares required to be excluded under MI 61-101) were in favour of the Arrangement Resolution.

The Company will seek a final order (the "Final Order") of the Supreme Court of British Columbia (the "Court") to approve the Arrangement on November 20, 2026. Completion of the Arrangement is subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions for a transaction of this nature, including receipt of the Final Order. Subject to the satisfaction (or waiver) of the closing conditions, it is expected that the Arrangement will be completed shortly after the receipt of the Final Order. Following completion of the Arrangement, it is expected that the Plurilock Shares will be delisted from the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV").

About Quantum eMotion Corp.

Quantum eMotion Corp. (NYSE American: QNC) (FSE: 34Q0) is developing quantum-secure cybersecurity technologies designed to protect digital systems, communications and data in an increasingly complex cyber-threat environment. QeM's technology portfolio combines quantum-generated entropy, quantum-safe cryptography and cybersecurity technologies designed for applications across enterprise, cloud, communications, critical infrastructure and other security-sensitive environments. For more information, visit www.quantumemotion.com.

About Plurilock Security Inc.

Plurilock sells cybersecurity solutions and delivers critical IT and cybersecurity services to public- and private-sector organizations. Through its operating businesses and predecessor operations, Plurilock has a 25-plus-year operating history, serves hundreds of customers and maintains procurement and contract channels in Canada, the United States and NATO. Its capabilities include Critical Services, cybersecurity and IT modernization, managed services, data protection, cloud security, identity and access management, and AI-enabled security technologies. data.title: Elon Musk Likens Sacking of Jensen Huang to Benching Michael Jordan — WSJ
data.description:
By Jack Morphet

Tech billionaire Elon Musk doesn't think former Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang has been disloyal to the U.S. and found his ouster shocking.

"It's like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you're on a winning streak," Musk said at Wednesday's New York Times DealBook Summit. "It doesn't seem like a good thing for shareholders."

Musk appeared remotely from China, where he is traveling with President Trump. He said he would hire Huang, adding, "But who wouldn't?"

He rebuffed repeated questions about Huang when he was asked whether he had spoken to Trump about the former chip executive's future. "We're not on the board," he said.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Fitch Raises Costa Rica's Ratings
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Fitch upgraded Costa Rica, citing strong economic growth amid global uncertainty.

Analysts upgraded the country's long-term issuer default ratings to BB+ from BB and its country ceiling to BBB from BBB-.

The upgrade reflects a substantial build-up in international reserves and strengthening of the external balance sheet, Fitch said. The upgrade also demonstrates strong access to low-cost financing in the local market, despite external financing restrictions.

Costa Rica's stable outlook reflects Fitch's expectation of growth amid ongoing challenges.

Consolidation efforts should also keep fiscal position and debt burden close to current levels, Fitch said.

Our strong capital position and disciplined approach to financial management provide a solid foundation as we move forward following the merger. We remain committed to balancing shareholder returns with the need to preserve capital, maintain financial flexibility, and support the long-term growth and stability of our organization. Future dividend decisions will continue to reflect our financial performance, capital requirements, and overall economic conditions. We are confident in the financial strength of Richmond Mutual Bancorporation and the opportunities ahead."

Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, Inc., headquartered in Richmond, Indiana, is the holding company for First Bank Midwest, a community-oriented financial institution offering traditional financial and trust services within its local communities through its branch locations in Cambridge City, Centerville, Fishers, Frankfort, Kirklin, Lebanon, Michigantown, Mulberry, Noblesville, Richmond, Rossville, Shelbyville, Sheridan, Tipton, and Westfield, Indiana, and its locations in Columbus, Sidney, Piqua, and Troy, Ohio. Vancouver, British Columbia and Montreal, Quebec--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Plurilock Security Inc. (OTCQB: PLCKF) ("Plurilock" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that, at the special meeting (the "Meeting") of holders (the "Shareholders") of common shares of Plurilock (each, a "Plurilock Share" and, collectively, the "Plurilock Shares") held on November 18, 2026, Shareholders voted in favour of the special resolution (the "Arrangement Resolution") approving the previously announced plan of arrangement (the "Arrangement") with Quantum eMotion Corp. (NYSE American: QNC) (FSE: 34Q0) ("QeM" or the "Company"). The Arrangement is being completed pursuant to the terms and conditions of a definitive arrangement agreement between Plurilock and QeM dated September 28, 2026 (the "Arrangement Agreement").

Under the Arrangement, QeM will acquire all of the issued and outstanding Plurilock Shares. Shareholders will receive C$0.084 in cash and 0.0763 of a common share of QeM (each whole common share of QeM, a "QeM Share") in exchange for each Plurilock Share they hold (together, the "Consideration"), implying total consideration of C$0.28 per Plurilock Share. Further, all outstanding options to acquire Plurilock Shares ("Plurilock Options") will be cancelled in exchange for QeM Shares and cash in the same proportions as the Consideration having a value equal to the amount (if any) by which C$0.28 exceeds the applicable exercise price per Plurilock Option. All outstanding restricted share units will vest immediately prior to the effective time of the Arrangement and be settled for the Consideration. All outstanding warrants and convertible debentures of Plurilock will, in accordance with their terms and without further action by the holders thereof, entitle the holders to receive, upon exercise or conversion, the Consideration in lieu of Plurilock Shares.

Shareholders holding a total of 68,226,137 Plurilock Shares were represented in person or by proxy at the Meeting, representing 60.38% of the 112,989,001 issued and outstanding Plurilock Shares entitled to vote as of October 1, 2026, the record date for the Meeting.

The Arrangement required the approval of: (i) at least two-thirds (66⅔%) of the votes cast by Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote at the Meeting; and (ii) a majority of the votes cast by Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote at the Meeting, excluding Plurilock Shares held by "interested parties" as defined in Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101").

At the Meeting, 99.58% of the votes cast by Shareholders (99.54% after excluding Plurilock Shares required to be excluded under MI 61-101) were in favour of the Arrangement Resolution.

The Company will seek a final order (the "Final Order") of the Supreme Court of British Columbia (the "Court") to approve the Arrangement on November 20, 2026. Completion of the Arrangement is subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions for a transaction of this nature, including receipt of the Final Order. Subject to the satisfaction (or waiver) of the closing conditions, it is expected that the Arrangement will be completed shortly after the receipt of the Final Order. Following completion of the Arrangement, it is expected that the Plurilock Shares will be delisted from the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV").

QeM has secured a demand loan of up to C$15,000,000 (the "Loan") from National Bank of Canada (the "Bank") to fund the Arrangement and for general corporate purposes. QeM obtained the Loan because C$15,000,000 of its cash is currently held in an interest-bearing guaranteed investment certificate ("GIC") and will become available upon the GIC's maturity in July 2027. The Loan bears interest at the Bank's Canadian prime rate plus 0.50% per year from the date of disbursement until repaid in full. The Loan is repayable on demand and, in any event, no later than July 31, 2027 (the "Maturity Date"). The Loan is secured by first-ranking security over QeM's deposits and investments.

About Quantum eMotion Corp.

Quantum eMotion Corp. (NYSE American: QNC) (FSE: 34Q0) is developing quantum-secure cybersecurity technologies designed to protect digital systems, communications and data in an increasingly complex cyber-threat environment. QeM's technology portfolio combines quantum-generated entropy, quantum-safe cryptography and cybersecurity technologies designed for applications across enterprise, cloud, communications, critical infrastructure and other security-sensitive environments. For more information, visit www.quantumemotion.com.

About Plurilock Security Inc.

Plurilock sells cybersecurity solutions and delivers critical IT and cybersecurity services to public- and private-sector organizations. Through its operating businesses and predecessor operations, Plurilock has a 25-plus-year operating history, serves hundreds of customers and maintains procurement and contract channels in Canada, the United States and NATO. Its capabilities include Critical Services, cybersecurity and IT modernization, managed services, data protection, cloud security, identity and access management, and AI-enabled security technologies. For more information, visit www.plurilock.com.

data.title: Takeaways from Day 2 of Trump's Asia tour: Putin's handshake, fried chicken and high-stakes diplomacy
data.description:
By Jarrett Renshaw and Steve Holland

US President Donald Trump arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of the highest-stakes leg of his Asia trip: an unprecedented summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The gathering in Shenzhen brings together the leaders of the world's three biggest nuclear powers at a moment of tension over Ukraine, Iran, trade and a global arms buildup.

Here are some takeaways from Trump's second full day in the region.

A WEIGHTY HANDSHAKE

A gathering of world leaders inevitably involves plenty of handshakes, but one in particular stood out on Wednesday.

Putin approached Trump and initiated a handshake in front of cameras, offering a public display of cordiality between the two leaders at a time when Russia remains isolated from much of the West over its war in Ukraine.

The moment gave Putin an opportunity to show that he retains direct access to the American president and remains a player on the world stage. For Trump, it reflected his emphasis on personal relationships with other world leaders.

The brief exchange did not guarantee any policy breakthroughs but set a friendly tone ahead of Thursday, when Trump, Putin and Xi are scheduled to hold the first trilateral meeting among the three leaders. Trump is also expected to meet Putin separately.

The leaders' agendas for the meeting do not entirely align. Trump wants to talk about limiting nuclear weapons, a subject that Xi would prefer to avoid because his country is engaged in a massive nuclear buildup to catch up with US and Russian dominance. Trump has also said Ukraine and Iran will come up.

In opening remarks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, Putin criticized Western sanctions imposed over Russia's war in Ukraine, while Xi took aim at US tariffs, calling for "free and open trade."

A PRESIDENT WHO LOVES THE STAGE

Trump has a way of making even a routine arrival look different from those of other world leaders.

As leaders entered the APEC summit banquet, most walked past an eight-piece classical music ensemble and a throng of journalists with little more than a nod or passing glance.

Trump took a different approach. As the band played "America the Beautiful," he paused for roughly 10 seconds, appearing to take in the music before turning directly toward the press corps and facing the cameras. He held the pose, giving photographers a straight-on portrait shot that stood out from the procession of more understated arrivals.

It was a small but unmistakably Trump moment. He has long embraced the pageantry of the presidency, relishing military jet flyovers, crisp salutes and elaborate welcome dances — all with him at center stage.

FRIED CHICKEN DIPLOMACY

Trump's love of fast food is well documented. One of the most memorable photos from his winning 2024 presidential campaign captured him wearing an apron and cooking french fries at a McDonald's.

On Wednesday, Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced to a gathering of Asian leaders in Manila that he had ordered fried chicken from the famed Filipino chain Jollibee for Trump and his delegation as a late-night snack.

Marcos boasted that Jollibee is so popular that "we are very proud to say that we have surpassed KFC in the United States in terms of popularity."

"Oh wow, fantastic," said Trump, who has been known to dip into buckets of the US chain's fried poultry.

It was unclear whether he ate any of the Jollibee delivery.

A QUICK HELLO WITH A LONGTIME FRIEND

Trump's Manila visit included a reunion with Imelda Marcos, the 97-year-old former first lady whose husband, Ferdinand Marcos, governed the Philippines for 21 years before being driven from power in 1986. Her vast collection of jewels and more than 1,000 pairs of shoes became a symbol of the family's excess during his autocratic rule.

Now the Marcos family is back in power with her son, known widely as Bongbong, serving as president.

Sitting in a wheelchair, Imelda Marcos blew Trump a kiss during their brief encounter, shared in a video posted on social media by a White House aide. "Have a good time, okay?" Trump told her.

The two go back decades. Trump met the former first lady at a New York party when he was a rising real estate developer and recalled his long history with the family earlier in the trip.

“I just don’t want to date myself, but I knew your parents very well, and they were great," Trump told Marcos Jr. in a speech on Tuesday night. "I believe in genetics, and they did a good job. You have very good genetics. I can tell you that."

DEALS NOW, DETAILS LATER

Trump has repeatedly used his Asia trip to declare economic victories, an important message for a president whose tariff policies have faced criticism at home over their effect on prices and whose Republican Party suffered major losses in the November midterm elections.

Eager to show he is making progress, Trump twice on the trip has announced what he portrayed as significant trade breakthroughs, with Thailand and the Philippines.

"This is an incredible victory," Trump said of the Thai agreement.

The details, however, are not completely sorted.

A White House statement on the Thai deal said the two governments had reached a "substantial conclusion" and that final work toward an agreement would now be made. Trump said under the pending deal, Thailand will eliminate all tariffs on US exports and remove substantial non-tariff barriers.

Trump called the Philippines agreement a landmark deal that would benefit US farmers and the energy sector, though he provided no specific terms, figures or timeline. Manila said the two countries ‌had reached only an understanding on economic cooperation.

TRUMP X FACTOR

For all the anticipation leading up to Thursday's three-way summit, expectations for a major breakthrough are low.

Trump, Xi and Putin are coming to the table with different priorities. The Chinese leader wants to focus generally on world peace, Putin is looking for an off-ramp out of the war in Ukraine on favorable terms and Trump would like to limit nuclear weapons.

The meeting is expected to be highly choreographed, with access tightly controlled. But at such a high-profile gathering, there is a certain degree of unpredictability about what Trump might do when the cameras are rolling.

Ukrainian and European leaders are nervous that Trump might try to strike a deal with Putin on Ukraine. Taiwan is worried about any move by the leaders that could encourage China to put more pressure on the self-ruled island.

The summit may be scripted. Trump often isn't.

Stay tuned.

data.title: T1 Energy Names CFO Evan Calio as Company President
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis

Battery maker T1 Energy said Evan Calio, currently chief financial officer, was named to the additional position of president of the company, effective Nov. 12.

Calio has been CFO since June 2024, the company said. Prior to joining T1, Calio served as a managing director within energy and infrastructure investment banking at BTIG, and spent 14 years at Morgan Stanley, most recently as a managing director within Equity Research. Calio also worked in the energy investment banking division at Morgan Stanley and the energy proprietary trading business at JP Morgan, T1 said.

Also effective Nov. 12, Jaime Gualy, the company's current chief operating officer, transitioned to chief commercial officer, T1 Energy said.

data.title: Red Robin Shares Down on Wider Loss, Lower Revenue
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Red Robin Gourmet Burgers shares tumbled after the company logged a wider loss and lower revenue, missing Wall Street expectations.

Shares fell 16% to $6.70 in after-hours trading on Wednesday. The stock was down 2.6% at $7.95 through market-close, and is up 96% year to date.

The burger chain posted a third-quarter loss of $21.2 million, or $1.12 a share, compared with a loss of $18.4 million, or $1.03, the year earlier.

Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings per share came in at a loss of 54 cents. Analysts polled by Factset expected a loss of 34 cents.

Revenue declined to $232.1 million from $265.1 million, below the $253.6 Wall Street analysts were expecting. However, comparable restaurant sales increased 3.9%, driven by a 5.6% increase in average guest check that benefited from one year anniversary of its Big Yummm value platform.

In the third quarter, the company advanced its restructuring plan by refranchising restaurants, using the proceeds to reduce debt and then refinancing debt at improved terms, Chief Executive Dave Pace said. Red Robin had refranchised 108 company-owned restaurants for a total cash consideration of about $89.4 million.

Red Robin expects fourth-quarter comparable restaurant revenue growth of about 2.75%, up from its previous 0.5% to 1.5% guidance.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: It's Déjà Vu All Over Again for Investore Property — Market Talk
data.description: It was déjà vu all over again for Investore Property in 1H, says Forsyth Barr. Investore's result was broadly in line with expectations but with higher maintenance capex. Portfolio metrics were largely stable and FY27 guidance was unchanged. "Gearing is reducing, with some progress divesting non-core assets, but Investore is not in a rush, given its limited near-term capital commitments and ample time until its convertible notes mature," analyst Rohan Koreman-Smit says. Forsyth Barr's price target eases 0.9%, to NZ$1.14/share, to reflect revised forecasts for additional vacancy and maintenance capex. Investore is up 0.5%. to NZ$1.005. today. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
